instances.title: SSH Simulator Instances
instances.subtitle: Linux and network-device simulators with per-instance local or LAN access.
instances.noInstances: No instances yet. Create a Linux or network device to begin.

instances.deleteConfirm: Delete {{name}}? This also removes its local state and host key.
instances.createSubtitle: Configure one login account and choose password, public-key, or combined authentication.
instances.endpointSettingsHint: Change the listen scope or port. Saving starts the instance immediately.
instances.lanWarningTitle: Other devices will be able to connect
instances.lanWarning: The instance will listen on every network interface. Use a strong password or SSH key, and allow only trusted networks through Windows Firewall.
instances.networkAccessReady: LAN listening is enabled. Replace HOST_IP in the connection command with this computer's LAN address.
instances.lanAccessEnabled: At least one instance accepts LAN connections
instances.connectFromLan: Other devices can connect with {{command}}; HOST_IP is the LAN address of the computer running MonolithSSH.

authHint.publickey: Better for scripts and external SSH clients

instances.passwordHint: Set your own value or generate a strong random password.
instances.publicKeyHint: Paste an OpenSSH public key or generate a new key pair locally.
instances.credentialsReadyHint: {{name}} was created. You can revisit its credentials from Connection info at any time.
instances.hostIpHint: Replace HOST_IP with the LAN address of the computer running MonolithSSH.
instances.passwordCredentialHint: The password stays hidden until you explicitly reveal it.
instances.keyCredentialHint: This instance has {{count}} authorized public key(s).
instances.managedPrivateKeyHint: The private key is encrypted with operating-system secure storage and is not displayed directly.
instances.externalPrivateKeyHint: Only the authorized public key is stored here. Its matching private key is held externally and cannot be displayed or exported by the app.
instances.privateKeyWarning: The private key is encrypted locally for the built-in terminal and can be exported again from Connection info.
instances.externalKeyHint: This instance uses your supplied public key. Connect externally with its matching private key.
instances.terminalUnavailable: No local private key matches this external public key. Use an external SSH client.

terminal.title: Remote Terminal
terminal.subtitle: Real SSH sessions rendered with xterm.js.
terminal.noRunningHint: Start or create a local Linux or network-device simulator first.
terminal.previewHint: Run the Electron application to connect to the real local SSH service.
terminal.previewHelp: Electron mode supports real Linux and network-device sessions.

settings.title: MCP SSE Interface
settings.subtitle: Let local MCP clients control MonolithSSH through a stateless surface you can disable at any time.
settings.gatewayHint: Bound to 127.0.0.1 only. MCP clients can call application capabilities while enabled.
settings.localOnlyHint: Always binds to 127.0.0.1 and validates Host and Origin.
settings.appOwnsStateHint: Instances, rules, and variables remain managed by MonolithSSH services.
settings.ephemeralConnectionsHint: Legacy SSE connections live only in memory and disappear on disconnect.
settings.jsonHint: Add this configuration to an MCP client that supports the legacy SSE transport.
settings.capabilitiesHint: 20 tools validate inputs before calling the app service. The gateway adds no database and caches no business results.
settings.fullControlHint: While enabled, trusted MCP clients can manage instances, listen endpoints, authentication, rules, variables, built-ins, and audit data. Secrets are redacted unless includeSecrets is explicit, and managed private keys are never returned through MCP.

tools.instancesHint: List, inspect, create, start, stop, and delete SSH instances.
tools.credentialsHint: Read connection details or update users, passwords, and authorized keys; passwords are redacted by default.
tools.diagnosticsHint: Check ports and owning processes, or move an instance to an available port and start it.
tools.commandsHint: Run one non-interactive command on a running instance and read its result.
tools.rulesHint: Read or replace type-level and device-level rules with immediate effect.
tools.variablesHint: Read or replace custom variables; secret values are redacted by default.
tools.builtinsHint: Inspect, enable, disable, or restore the default built-in commands.
tools.auditHint: Filter audit events by instance, type, result, source, time, and search text.

profiles.rulesHint: Define command parsing and responses for this mode.
profiles.hotReloadHint: Device rules override type rules; after saving, the next command in existing sessions uses the new rules.
profiles.typeRulesHint: Every device of this type uses these rules. A device-level rule with the same command can override them.
profiles.deviceRulesHint: These rules apply only to this device and take priority over type-level rules and built-ins.
profiles.noRulesHint: Built-in commands remain available. Registered commands match first as an override layer.
profiles.outputPlaceholder: Enter the response returned when this command runs...
profiles.interactionFlowHint: Steps run in order. Input steps pause until the client responds.
profiles.finishHint: End the interaction here and display the current session prompt.
profiles.collectInputHint: Pause the shell and wait for one response.
profiles.verifyInputHint: Compare the response with a managed variable.
profiles.changeStateHint: Run a controlled action after verification succeeds.
profiles.optionalOutput: Optional; leave blank for a clean prompt
profiles.variableLiveHint: Saved values are used by the next command in existing SSH sessions. Secret input is never written to audit logs.
profiles.systemVariablesHint: Read-only values supplied by the current command and SSH session.

systemVariableDescriptions.user: Current session user, including a user selected by su.
systemVariableDescriptions.command: Complete command line entered by the client.
systemVariableDescriptions.arg1: First argument after the matched command.
systemVariableDescriptions.input: Response collected by an interactive rule.

profiles.customVariablesHint: Persistent values available to output templates and interactive verification.
profiles.variableDescriptionPlaceholder: Describe where this value is used
profiles.noVariablesHint: Add a value for output templates or interactive rule verification.
profiles.invalidVariableName: Variable names must start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, numbers, dots, hyphens or underscores.
profiles.variableInUseMissing: Variable {{name}} is still used by an interactive rule.
profiles.patternRequired: Every command rule must include a command or expression.
profiles.interactionStepsRequired: Interactive rules require at least one step.
profiles.finishMustBeLast: Finish must be the final interaction step.
profiles.missingInputReference: Interaction input {{name}} has not been collected by an earlier step.
profiles.builtinLiveHint: Deleted commands stop working immediately in existing Linux sessions. Restore resets the full default catalog.
profiles.builtinCatalogHint: These commands are provided by the Linux simulator engine. Custom rules still have higher matching priority.
profiles.noBuiltinsHint: Restore the complete default Linux command catalog with one action.

builtinDescriptions.exit: Exit the current shell, including the logout alias.
builtinDescriptions.help: List the built-in commands that are currently enabled.
builtinDescriptions.id: Show the current user and group identifiers.
builtinDescriptions.date: Show the current date and time.
builtinDescriptions.uname: Show Linux kernel and system information.
builtinDescriptions.env: Print the simulated shell environment variables.
builtinDescriptions.ip: Show virtual network addresses or the routing table.
builtinDescriptions.systemctl: Show the simulated SSH service status.
builtinDescriptions.cd: Change the current virtual filesystem directory.
builtinDescriptions.ls: List a virtual directory or file.
builtinDescriptions.touch: Create an empty file or preserve an existing file.
builtinDescriptions.rm: Remove a virtual file or directory entry.
builtinDescriptions.echo: Print text or redirect it into a virtual file.
builtinDescriptions.uptime: Show simulated host uptime and load averages.
builtinDescriptions.which: Resolve the virtual path of an enabled built-in command.
